subject: English
passage: Researchers wanted to test how teenagers respond to different types of feedback on their work. In an experiment, two instructors provided feedback on student presentations while teenagers (ages thirteen to sixteen) observed. Both instructors gave the same constructive criticism, but one of them also offered specific suggestions for improvement. When asked which instructor they would prefer to work with, 68% chose the instructor who provided specific suggestions. The researchers think that offering concrete advice showed the teenagers that the instructor was genuinely invested in helping them succeed. The teenagers may have perceived the instructor who gave only general criticism as less supportive.
prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: An experiment showed that the type of feedback given may influence whether teenagers view an instructor as supportive.
choices.B: Researchers think teenagers cannot benefit from constructive criticism until they are sixteen years old.
choices.C: An experiment found that providing specific suggestions is the best way to teach presentation skills to teenagers.
choices.D: Researchers think teenagers expect to receive praise when the teenagers demonstrate that they are willing to accept feedback.

explanation:
Choice A is the best answer. The text describes a study examining how teenagers respond to different feedback types and its results. It concludes that the teenagers in the study may have thought that an instructor who provided specific suggestions was more supportive than an instructor who gave only general criticism.

Why C is incorrect:

Choice C is incorrect. The experiment wasn't about teaching presentation skills—rather, it was about how different types of feedback affected the teenagers' perception of instructor supportiveness.
